    Biserial modules #

    The radical of a biserial module is the sum of at most two uniserial submodules whose intersection is simple or zero. Zero summands are allowed, so the definition also covers uniserial and semisimple local modules without separate edge cases.

          IsUniserialModule R M

          If a simple-top module is biserial and its radical again has simple top, then it is uniserial. Indeed, the two biserial branches cannot both be proper in the radical, since every proper submodule of a simple-top module lies in its Jacobson radical.
